notes: Sites enumerated 2026-10-07 on dev ac7593c60 from lock_discipline_check's own R2 region walk (a probe copy recording each (lock, leaf) site), grouped by the call that reaches the unlink:

Fix shape: every unlink here removes a superseded name after the durable rename/link that replaced it (cleanup, not the commit point). Defer it to an off-mutex debt list drained after the lock is released, the pattern fnn-immutable-close-debts already uses (LOCK-R1B-IMMUTABLE-CLOSE-DEBT-UNLOCKED fixed its locking), with crash recovery already tolerating a leftover superseded name (verify per family before moving). Group (a) rides with LOCK-R2-LIVE-RECONFIGURE-IO's design; (b)-(e) are C's lane after it. Gate per family: its sites leave the O count, no new key, REAL-key guard, host_check --load/--read 0, natives listed for convergence.

lock-io-out statement (application/receipt immutable stages): O stages an exact cleanup record (stage path, cleanup directory, operation label) only after fn-jpub reaches its terminal authority result. The section unwind drains cleanup off O/E; a cleanup mutex atomically changes :pending to :calling before unlink/fsync, then rechecks the exact receipt before removing it. Other drainers cannot take a calling record. Cleanup does not change the ACL2 publication result and recovery already sweeps surviving random private stage names. The unmodified live-reconfigure callers (including auth bindings and redeem) remain with deputy P. Log spare disposal has a deterministic reusable name and is audited separately; it cannot use this random-stage cleanup queue.

lock-io-out statement (log rotation): O/K stage rejected-spare disposal by atomically taking the spare slot and installing its existing physical close-debt receipt under the spare-slot lock. The queued receipt reserves the deterministic pathname: another prepare/take sees the pending custody refusal and cannot create a replacement. After O/K release, close/lstat/unlink run once; the spare-slot lock rechecks receipt identity and clears debt only on success, otherwise retains the exact condition. The section boundary classifies cleanup failures with its carried failure context. ACL2’s rotation admission, index and result are unchanged; only physical custody/cleanup moves.

lock-io-out result: workflow.lisp calls fnn-immutable-publish-deferred; owner section unwind and standalone application-journal unwind drain exact cleanup receipts. io.lisp rotation now stages rejected-spare custody, reserves its deterministic name in close-debt, then the post-section/offline rotate unwind calls the existing physical closer off O/K and settles the receipt. O unlink sites 24 -> 10; K unlink key gone; E stays at 1. All remaining O/E sites are live reconfiguration, including auth bindings and redeem, which stay with deputy P. The O key is no longer NEW (below the unchanged baseline 17); it remains a finding at 10, not a claim of zero. No ACL2-decision blocker found. Natives owed: tests/test_native_ion_workflow.py, tests/test_native_ion_receipt_recovery.py, tests/test_native_bp_carry_abandon.py, tests/test_native_log.py, tests/test_native_checkpoint_auto.py, tests/test_native_snapshot_bless.py. Add blocked-unlink/concurrent-prepare and close-error/no-retry schedules at convergence.

lock-io-out statement (administrative stages, superseding the earlier remaining-site boundary): the last 10 O and 1 E unlink sites all share fnn-admin-publish’s post-authority cleanup, including auth bindings and redeem. That cleanup can use the same deferred immutable receipt without changing deputy P’s live-reconfiguration decisions or other I/O. fnn-admin-publish stages cleanup while O/E remain held; the section unwind drains after both release and rechecks receipt ownership under the cleanup mutex. Standalone fnn-admin-publish-record drains in its off-mutex unwind after readback. Concurrent sections see the already-complete ACL2 publication; no field from the publication is recomputed by the host, and only the unused random stage name is removed.

lock-io-out final scope/result: the administrative publisher now also stages its cleanup; fnn-admin-publish-record drains its standalone path after readback. No live-reconfiguration phase decision or other I/O moved. All fnn-unlink findings under O/E/K are gone (O 24 -> 0, E 1 -> 0, K 1 -> 0), superseding the earlier 10-site remainder. NEW-set comparison to the supplied 60-key brief removes the O and E unlink keys.
